title: Nolan's The Odyssey Opens to $264 Million Worldwide, His Biggest Debut Ever
excerpt: The first film shot entirely on IMAX cameras earned $124.5 million domestically, outpacing Star Wars, Minions, and DC Universe franchise entries.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Odyssey grossed $264.1 million globally, marking Nolan's biggest debut ever.
  • The film cost $250 million to produce and is shot entirely on IMAX cameras.
  • It earned an A CinemaScore and a 97% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes.
  • 53% of attendees cited Nolan as their main reason for seeing the film.
  • Analysts predict it could surpass $1 billion globally, a first since The Dark Knight Rises.

  • Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey grossed $264.1 million globally in its opening weekend, including $124.5 million in North America — the director's biggest worldwide debut ever
  • The nearly three-hour, R-rated epic based on Homer's poem cost $250 million to produce and was the first major studio film shot entirely on IMAX cameras
  • The film earned an A CinemaScore and 97% Rotten Tomatoes audience score, with 53% of attendees citing Nolan as their primary reason for seeing it
  • Industry analysts project The Odyssey could become Nolan's first film since The Dark Knight Rises in 2012 to surpass $1 billion globally

Christopher Nolan has done it again. His adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey opened to $264.1 million in worldwide ticket sales over the weekend, Universal Pictures said on Sunday — the biggest global debut of the director's career and a decisive validation of Hollywood's growing bet on filmmaker-driven blockbusters.

The film earned $124.5 million in North America, making it the third-largest domestic opening of 2026 behind Toy Story 5 and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, and the year's biggest for any live-action release, according to studio estimates released by Rentrak. Internationally, The Odyssey posted the second-largest R-rated opening of all time, behind only 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine.

Nolan's Brand Power Defies Convention

That a nearly three-hour, R-rated adaptation of an ancient Greek poem could open bigger than recent entries in the Star Wars, Minions, and DC Universe franchises speaks to a fundamental shift in Hollywood economics. According to data from Rentrak provided by Universal, 53% of The Odyssey attendees said the director was their No. 1 reason for seeing the film.

"It's not often you see that. Chris Nolan has earned the audience's trust and respect."

— Jim Orr, Universal Pictures President of Domestic Distribution

"Studios are lost as far as knowing what works and what doesn't," said Bryan Lourd, chief executive of Creative Artists Agency, in an interview with the Wall Street Journal. "Things have generationally changed and individual, singular voices are taking advantage."

A Record-Breaking IMAX Achievement

The film made history as the first major studio production shot entirely using IMAX cameras. Nolan approached IMAX directly about the idea. "I went to IMAX, and I said, 'Look, if ever we are going to fulfil this dream of shooting the entire movie that way, this is the one,'" he told NBC's Today show. "This is The Odyssey."

The gamble paid off: IMAX screens generated nearly 20% of the global gross despite representing less than 1% of all auditoriums worldwide, according to the Wall Street Journal. Premium screens of all types in the U.S. and Canada accounted for 45% of tickets sold, according to research firm EntTelligence. Demand for IMAX 70mm showings was so intense that more than 50 theaters across North America added screenings between midnight and 7 a.m.

The Cast and the Odyssey Itself

Matt Damon leads the film as Odysseus, joined by Tom Holland, Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Anne Hathaway, Lupita Nyong'o, Charlize Theron, Elliot Page, Jon Bernthal, Mia Goth, and Indian-origin British actor Himesh Patel. The $250 million production was shot across Europe with largely practical visual effects, including a 35-foot-tall Trojan Horse.

Nolan's film centers on a portion of Odysseus's homecoming from the Trojan War — his encounters with gods, monsters, storms, and tragedy. The source material, attributed to Homer and believed to date from the seventh or eighth century BC, had never been adapted at this scale for the big screen.

What It Means for India and the Diaspora

The Odyssey opened to Rs 18 crore on its first day in India, breaking Nolan's own record for the biggest debut by one of his films in the country. Himesh Patel's prominent role has generated particular interest among Indian and South Asian audiences. The film continues to play on IMAX screens globally, with premium-format tickets likely to remain in high demand for weeks.

What's Next

With overwhelmingly positive reviews and an A CinemaScore, The Odyssey is projected to have strong legs through the summer. Industry analysts believe it could become Nolan's first film to surpass $1 billion globally since The Dark Knight Rises in 2012. Oppenheimer, his previous film, earned $976 million worldwide and won seven Academy Awards including best picture and best director.

In his interview with Today, Nolan confirmed it will be "at least" three years before his next film reaches theaters — consistent with the three-year cadence he has maintained since 2014.
